cdn_compression.aggregate_note: The aggregate is BYTE-WEIGHTED (sum of unique uncompressed sizes over sum of unique compressed sizes), so the LARGEST paths dominate it. Read per_path_distribution for every point.
cdn_compression.note: How much the cache compresses NARs: uncompressed NarSize : actually-downloaded compressed transport bytes, exact rational, on real cache.nixos.org over verified TLS. This is a COMPRESSION-ratio finding. It is NOT a peer-vs-CDN transport comparison -- the peer's shipped transport is ALSO compressed (see peer_vs_cdn_transport).

peer_arm.byte_identity: NarHash-verified byte-identical peer fetch (VM byte oracle)
peer_arm.content: real cache.nixos.org store paths (identical to the CDN arm, joined by store_hash)
peer_arm.environment: real 3-node KVM LAN VM link (router+provider+consumer, mDNS+kad); multi-host beyond netns

peer_vs_cdn_transport.comparison: peer_wire_transport_bytes (REAL /nar/4 response protocol bytes: per-64-KiB-leaf zstd-3 + Bao proof + framing, measured from the provider serve over a real multi-host KVM link) : cdn_compressed_transport_bytes (REAL cache.nixos.org compressed download over verified TLS) -- IDENTICAL content per store_hash (uncompressed NarSize asserted equal across arms).
peer_vs_cdn_transport.finding: SUPPLEMENT: on every compared path the peer's /nar/4 zstd wire transport is >= the CDN's compressed transport (peers move comparable-to-MORE bytes, not fewer). The peer's value is locality / offload / CDN-independence, NOT a transport-byte win. The gap is the fast per-serve zstd-3 the peer regenerates on the fly vs the cache's once-off high-level whole-NAR zstd.
peer_vs_cdn_transport.units_note: Both sides are COMPRESSED wire transport bytes for the SAME NAR (apples to apples). This is NOT the uncompressed NarSize and NOT a compression ratio.

wall_clock_comparison.reason: peer transfer (real KVM VM link) and CDN download (single TCP stream over the public internet) are different links -- not a paired trial. The CDN wall clock is a SINGLE-STREAM lower bound on nix's real (parallel) CDN throughput and must not drive a speed-win claim. No sign, no delta; read the wall clocks as separate magnitudes. The load-bearing, link-independent finding is peer_vs_cdn_transport (BYTES).
